subject: Re: Short-term capacity buffer & pricing safeguard request
messages:
From: Zara Reid <zara.reid@quickcommerce.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term capacity pressure this weekend — ask for temporary uplift

Hi Camila,

Quick note from our ops team: we have a marketing push going live this Friday that will spike inference usage for a 36-hour window. Our forecasted token consumption for the weekend is about 3.5x our committed quota. We expect it to be transient but the burst will cause latency-sensitive checkout flows to see higher throttling if we don't increase the rate cap.

Two asks: 1) Can Redwood provision a short-term, provisional capacity buffer for the weekend (and retroactively bill/prorate) so we don't hit hard rate limits? 2) If we do go over, is there a way to cap overrun charges or apply a one-time credit to smooth the impact — we are asking for a small graceband on the overrun while we finalize our committed tier uplift next month.

I'm attaching our June usage file for reference.

Appreciate any quick guidance — we need to decide by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Zara
Head of Growth, QuickCommerce

Attachments: usage_report_jun2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Zara Reid <zara.reid@quickcommerce.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term capacity pressure this weekend — ask for temporary uplift

Hi Zara — thanks for the heads up and for the usage file. We can help here. Quick summary of what I propose so we can move fast: 

- Provisional transient load buffer: provision a short-window uplift for the 36-hour spike with guaranteed fallback to your committed tier afterward.
- Provisional credit bucket (graceband): apply a one-time, customer-level credit that offsets the first X% of overrun charges tied to this specific event. 
- Usage smoothing commitment: QuickCommerce commits to a follow-up meeting next week to finalize a stepped-up committed tier or a short-term reserved capacity purchase.

I'll attach a one-page amendment (proposed_transient_buffer_amendment_v1.pdf) that outlines the uplift window, the provisional credit amount, and a billing/proration approach. If you approve, we can push the uplift live and follow up with DocuSign for the amendment.

One quick operational note: to protect latency SLOs we will enable a short-window throttle uplift rather than changing long-term routing policies. That means your requests will be handled on dedicated transient capacity where possible, with automated fallback.

If that sounds okay I'll need verbal approval from you today so our infra team can schedule the capacity.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: proposed_transient_buffer_amendment_v1.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Short-term capacity pressure this weekend — ask for temporary uplift

Camila — quick internal note before we confirm:

- I reviewed Zara's usage file. Event looks like a legitimate short-window spike rather than a sustained pattern.
- Approve provisional uplift with the following guardrails:
  * Uplift window capped to 48 hours starting at the timestamp they confirm.
  * Provisional credit (graceband) capped to $6k or 25% of the uplifted usage charges, whichever is lower.
  * Require QuickCommerce to sign the one-page amendment in DocuSign within 72 hours of uplift initiation — otherwise future overrun protection not guaranteed.

Aditya: can ops push the transient capacity if we get Zara's verbal OK? Also flagging that we should add a HubSpot task to follow up on committed tier upgrade by Aug 1.

-Vivek
VP, Sales Operations
